prompt:
You are the prosecutor. Your job is to FALSIFY the claims below. For each claim, either:
(a) state a concrete scenario in which it is false, AND propose a minimal test or command
    that would demonstrate it; or (b) state you could not falsify it.
You may also raise NEW hypotheses about behaviour the change silently alters.
Every hypothesis must cite exact diff lines. No confidence numbers.
note: Hypotheses only. A hypothesis counts as a finding only after the evidence engine runs its test_sketch and it reproduces. Nothing here was executed.

attacks.scenario: Nested closed generics from metadata: Outer<T> (referenced assembly) has a keyed member of type Inner<T> (also referenced). GetObjectInfo recurses through CollectGeneric once per closed generic, so any third null-unsafe lookup on that path would still throw although the two patched sites are safe.
attacks.test_sketch: In a scratch copy of GenericsFormatterTests.cs add: defineSource = 'using MessagePack; namespace Lib { [MessagePackObject] public struct Inner<T> { [Key(0)] public T V { get; set; } } [MessagePackObject] public struct Outer<T> { [Key(0)] public Inner<T> I { get; set; } } }'; usageSource = '[MessagePackObject] public class Use { [Key(0)] public Lib.Outer<int> O { get; set; } } [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class R { }'; await RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync(defineSource, usageSource, 'TempProject.R.g.cs').
attacks.holds_if: passes on head with no diagnostics

attacks.scenario: The resolver file is emitted but the formatter for the closed generic is missing or the generated code does not compile: the helper uses SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and asserts only that a hint name exists.
attacks.test_sketch: After RunGenerators in the helper, add generated trees to usageCompilation and assert compilation.GetDiagnostics() has no errors; then reflect over the emitted assembly and round-trip serialize Cmd with MessagePackSerializer using the generated resolver.
attacks.holds_if: no compile errors and the round-trip equals the input
attacks.falsified_if: compile error, or the resolver has no formatter for Item<int>

attacks.scenario: The four rows the issue lists as already working (struct, record struct, class<T>, record class<T>) have no regression test, so a change in their behaviour would not be noticed.
attacks.test_sketch: Parameterise RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync over the six declaration forms from the issue table, each declared in the referenced assembly, run on base and head, and compare crash/ok per row with the issue_matrix in REQ-2283.yaml.
attacks.holds_if: head: all six ok; base: exactly the two struct<T> forms crash
attacks.falsified_if: any other row differs between base and head

attacks.scenario: The constructor-level filter changes the set of reported diagnostics for source types. Candidate inputs are call sites whose location expression can be null for a source declaration: the formatter-attribute argument location, the colliding-names location and the partial-type primary location.
attacks.test_sketch: Create worktrees at base and head. Write a small harness that runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer through CompilationWithAnalyzers over every input in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests (markup stripped) and prints (diagnostic id, span) sorted. Run in both worktrees and diff the outputs; expected: identical for every source-only input.

Dynamic: an inaccessible [MessagePackObject] type declared in a referenced assembly and used as a member type: record whether InaccessibleDataType is reported on base and on head.

attacks.scenario: Roslyn rejects diagnostics whose location is a source location in a tree outside the compilation, but a diagnostic with Location.None or a metadata location is reportable. If so the comment's premise is false and the filter is broader than needed.
attacks.test_sketch: Write a minimal DiagnosticAnalyzer (inside the test project) that calls context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(descriptor, Location.None)) and one with a metadata location taken from a referenced type's Locations[0]; run it via CSharpAnalyzerVerifier. Expected if the comment is true: AD0001 or an exception. Expected if false: the diagnostic is reported without error.

cited_lines.quote: against a location that does not exist, which analyzers are not permitted to do.

attacks.scenario: A positional record whose primary-constructor property carries a key attribute with a null string value: the property syntax is a parameter, so 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax' is null, the location is Location.None, and the new filter drops the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic. On base the cast to PropertyDeclarationSyntax throws instead, so a crash becomes silence.
attacks.test_sketch: Analyzer test (VerifyCS): '[MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key((string)null)] string X);' Record on base: AD0001 with InvalidCastException expected; on head: no diagnostic and no exception.
attacks.holds_if: head reports a diagnostic at the parameter
attacks.falsified_if: head reports nothing (confirms the claim is false)
